newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Continental sees '96 Luz del Sur sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Continental sees '96 Luz del Sur sale.

text.p: Banco Continental, the bank leading the local portion of the placement of state-held shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur, expects the sale to go ahead before the end of the year, a bank executive said Monday.
"Always taking into account market conditions, the placement, in principle, will be this year," Banco Continental general manager, Jose Carlos Pla, said in an interview.
The Peruvian government, which holds a 30 percent stake in Luz del Sur, chose Banco Continental last week to lead a group of banks handling the local portion of the sale.
The bank overseeing the international portion of the placement will be selected September 10, privatization officials have said.
As part of the local sale directed by Banco Continental, Spain's Banco Santander has been selected to handle the placement with local institutions, according to the officials.
The bank's brokerage - Santander SAB - will direct a group of local brokerages to book build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks, they said.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc. and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc. bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
